items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: we had Old Man McCurtis, he's dead, Willie Humphrey, George Augustine on bass, Mercedes Goldman on piano... Professor John Robeshoe... I was on the drum

ctx.x: That time, with that band, was what Rick Howe was playing, Poison. And sometimes we had Piku with us. Yeah. Yeah. Mostly. Then we'd try to get Willie, but Willie was working with Paul Barber and sometimes with Fredrick Coleman, that. And the same block by Sid DeVille at Montegral. But we first started with Piku playing Clown and Poison. And we had a trombone player by the name of, he died not long ago. That man live uptown there. Not Piers? No, not late. What's his name?

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: Me and Poison Humphrey, we were just working together... Me and Poison Humphrey, we'd be playing together like that

ctx.x: Uh, so when did you go into Celestan?

Oh, yeah, I was playing, uh, let me see, then we, Me and Poison Humphrey, we were just working together. Them the fellas I forgot to mention. See, when we'd be living in the field, Me and Poison Humphrey, we'd be playing together like that, on and off, Em and all of us like that. And we decided to make that band strong, you know, just make, organize it like. Yeah. But Sweet Em and Esma, she used it. And the name first was titled from Miss Valente at the paddock. She's the one made Em use that adopted name of the…
